sentences.text:
Order 
This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.509 of 2024 of Vidyanagar Police Station, Kasaragod,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 468, 471, & 420 of the Indian Penal Code 3.

According to the prosecution, the accused had, during the period from 16.07.2019 to 05.11.2019,
forged ownership certificate and basic tax receipt and approached the Kerala Gramin Bank for obtaining a loan and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the entire prosecution allegations are false and the incident as 2025:KER:40624 alleged had not occurred.

It was further submitted that petitioner has no role in the alleged forgery and that he has been falsely implicated as the 10th accused in the aforesaid crime which itself would indicate that he is innocent and further that he is willing to abide by the conditions that may be imposed by this Court while granting him bail.

6. The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that petitioner is one of the main accused in the aforesaid crime and that he had forged ownership certificate and basic tax receipt for the benefit of other persons while he was serving as Special Village Officer and, therefore, custodial interrogation is essential.
7. Petitioner is alleged to have indulged in a serious offence of forgery and fabricated ownership certificate.
Though the petitioner is arrayed as the 10 th accused, the same is not determinative of the nature of offence committed by the accused.

Considering the nature of allegations raised against the petitioner and his alleged involvement in the crime, I am of the view that this is not a fit case where petitioner could be protected 2025:KER:40624 with an order of anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, this bail application is dismissed.
